elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The Company, corresponding to Customer, may expressly terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires ninety (90) days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is required; instead, the Company may owe a Termination Payment.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Any termination by HDI, corresponding to Vendor, is effective only at the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Company may terminate for convenience upon ninety (90) days' written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is capped at three (3) months of fees payable under Section 3.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that any termination by HDI under Section 4.1 is effective only at the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The retained bilateral termination language requires either Party, including HDI, to provide ninety (90) days' written notice.
